niveis.descricao: Você entende e usa frases do dia a dia, se apresenta e responde perguntas simples sobre você.
Você conversa sobre rotina, família e compras, e entende frases curtas quando a pessoa fala devagar.
Você se vira em viagens, conta experiências e dá opiniões simples. O próximo passo é ganhar fluidez.
Você discute temas variados com naturalidade e entende boa parte do inglês falado em ritmo normal.
Você se expressa com precisão, entende nuances e ironia e usa o inglês com segurança no trabalho e nos estudos.

I used to think that working from home would make me more productive, but honestly, it was the opposite. Without the commute, I ended up working longer hours, and I really missed the small conversations with colleagues. Now I go to the office three days a week, and that balance works much better for me.

audios.texto: What strikes me about the debate on screen time is how rarely we distinguish between different types of use. An hour spent video-calling a grandparent is hardly comparable to an hour of mindless scrolling, yet most guidelines lump them together. Until research accounts for that nuance, I'd take any blanket recommendation with a pinch of salt.

perguntas.enunciado: What is the speaker's main criticism?
alternativas: Guidelines treat all screen use as the same
There is no research on screens

escrita.tema: Write about your daily routine. What do you do in the morning, afternoon and evening? (40–80 words)
Describe your last vacation or a special weekend. Where did you go, who were you with and what did you do? (60–100 words)
Why do you want to improve your English? Tell me about a situation where English was important for you. (80–120 words)
Some people say remote work is the future. Do you agree? Give reasons and examples. (100–150 words)
"Social media does more harm than good." To what extent do you agree? Present a balanced argument. (120–180 words)
